findings.description: ARMED_DRIVER_KEY can be bypassed for git-lfs custom transfer agents: the check is case-sensitive and anchored, but git-lfs matches `customtransfer` case-insensitively and anywhere in the key, and also reads a URL-scoped standalonetransferagent.
findings.body:
**git-lfs transfer-agent keys can get past `ARMED_DRIVER_KEY` through case and placement**

`armedGitDrivers` tests the raw keys from `git config --list` against a pattern that is anchored and case-sensitive:

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/92149eb7dbf1692b2b93619ade67677bbe67d4c3/src/core/git-diff.client.ts#L313-L314

```ts
lfs\.customtransfer\..+\.(?:path|args)|lfs\.standalonetransferagent
```

Git keeps the subsection's case in `--list` output. So `git config lfs.CustomTransfer.pwn.path /tmp/pwn` lists as `lfs.CustomTransfer.pwn.path`, and that key passes the check. git-lfs still registers the agent, because it matches keys without regard to case and without anchoring (`tq/custom.go`):

```go
pathRegex := regexp.MustCompile(`lfs\.((?i)customtransfer\.([^.]+))\.path`)
for k, _ := range git.All() { match := pathRegex.FindStringSubmatch(k) ... path, _ := git.Get(k)
```

Two other forms also get past the check:
- a prefixed key such as `x.lfs.customtransfer.pwn.path`, which the unanchored regex still matches;
- `lfs.<url>.standalonetransferagent`, which git-lfs reads through `uc.Get("lfs", ep.Url, "standalonetransferagent")` in `tq/manifest.go`.

`GIT_SAFE_CONFIG` keeps git-lfs out of pup's own git calls. These keys still sit in the shared local config, though, and the operator's own `git lfs pull` reads them after a fast-forward, which is the step decision 82 tells the operator to take. A session can therefore plant a transfer agent without tripping the "second layer" refusal decision 82 describes.

Suggested fix: match what git-lfs actually accepts (see the suggestion). Adding `/i` to the `filter.` and `merge.` alternatives changes nothing, because git already lowercases section and variable names. The existing "names no program" cases still pass. Consider adding `lfs.CustomTransfer.pwn.path`, `x.lfs.customtransfer.pwn.path` and `lfs.https://example.com.standalonetransferagent` to the `it.each` in `src/core/git-diff-client.test.ts`.

*(git-lfs behaviour read from upstream `main` source; not run locally.)*

findings.description: Emptying `filter.lfs.*` in `GIT_SAFE_CONFIG` also changes `pup start`. In an LFS repo with a global `git lfs install`, `runGit(... 'worktree', 'add', '-b', ...)` used to give the session real LFS content. Now every new session worktree holds pointer files, and decision 82 only lists the gate checkout, the rebase and the fast-forward as affected.
findings.body:
**Session worktrees now start on LFS pointers, and decision 82 doesn't say so**

The new `filter.lfs.*` pins in `GIT_SAFE_CONFIG` apply to every `runGit` call, not just the gate's:

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/92149eb7dbf1692b2b93619ade67677bbe67d4c3/src/core/git-diff.client.ts#L78-L85

`pup start` creates the session worktree through `runGit`:

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/92149eb7dbf1692b2b93619ade67677bbe67d4c3/src/core/session-lifecycle.service.ts#L218

Take a repo whose `.gitattributes` uses `filter=lfs`, on a machine where the operator ran a global `git lfs install`. Before this PR, that `worktree add` smudged real LFS content into the session. Now the session's worktree holds pointer files. The conductor's graph checkout changes the same way:

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/92149eb7dbf1692b2b93619ade67677bbe67d4c3/src/core/conductor.service.ts#L80-L92

Decision 82 says "no pup git call runs git-lfs at all". Its consequence paragraph, though, lists only "the gate's checkout, the rebase and the fast-forward":

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/92149eb7dbf1692b2b93619ade67677bbe67d4c3/docs/09-decisions.md#L4197-L4207

So in an LFS repo whose build or tests need the binaries, a session now fails until someone runs `git lfs pull` inside the worktree, and pup gives no sign of why. The pull works there because the session's own git doesn't carry pup's `-c` pins. The new test (`git-diff-client.test.ts`) covers the gate and conductor `worktree add --detach` form, not the session's `-b` form.

Pinning at `worktree add` is defensible on security grounds, because another live session can write the shared config. So the fix is probably not to drop the pin. Please do one of these:
- extend decision 82 to cover session and conductor worktrees, and tell the session or operator to run `git lfs pull` (for example in the compiled profile or in `pup start`'s output);
- record why sessions should start without LFS content.

findings.description: with `--accept-debt`, several refusal messages say "Nothing was recorded as merged" or "nothing was merged", and `withLedgerKept` then appends "ledger entries were kept". The operator reads two statements that look contradictory.
findings.body:
**With `--accept-debt`, refusals say "nothing was recorded as merged" right before saying ledger entries were kept**

With `--accept-debt`, several refusals say "Nothing was recorded as merged". `withLedgerKept` then appends "The accepted-debt ledger entry was kept for the retry… this session is not merged." The entries it kept have descriptions that read "… merged from session X" (see `merge-gate.service.ts` L834, L897 and L909, and `debt.service.ts`). Decision 82 itself calls them "entries reading as merged". The operator therefore reads "nothing recorded as merged" next to a ledger entry that reads merged, which is the contradiction this PR set out to remove.

Each of these messages is raised after the ledger write, inside the `withLedgerKept` try blocks:
- [`github.client.ts` L188-L193](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/92149eb7dbf1692b2b93619ade67677bbe67d4c3/src/core/github.client.ts#L188-L193): `assertPullRequestHead` (new)
- [`merge-gate.service.ts` L488-L491](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/92149eb7dbf1692b2b93619ade67677bbe67d4c3/src/core/merge-gate.service.ts#L488-L491): `assertTargetAt`. The early call before the ledger write is fine, but the call from `fastForward` runs after it.
- [`merge-gate.service.ts` L537-L541](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/92149eb7dbf1692b2b93619ade67677bbe67d4c3/src/core/merge-gate.service.ts#L537-L541): the checkout failure in `fastForward`
- [`merge-gate.service.ts` L603-L607](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/92149eb7dbf1692b2b93619ade67677bbe67d4c3/src/core/merge-gate.service.ts#L603-L607): the compare-and-swap failure in `fastForward`

Suggested fix: say only what is true and make no claim about records:
- "The session is not merged" (or "Nothing was merged") in `assertPullRequestHead`;
- "nothing was checked out and the session is not merged" in `assertTargetAt`;
- "failed, and the session is not merged: …" for the compare-and-swap failure.

Each base message still reads correctly without the suffix, which is what you get when `--accept-debt` is off.

findings.description: The `commitSubjects` `git log` runs after the `--accept-debt` ledger write but outside both `withLedgerKept` try blocks, so a failure there (e.g. a session-written invalid `log.date`) leaves entries filed with no kept note; moving it above the ledger write closes the gap.
withLedgerKept's single-entry note reads "The accepted-debt ledger entry was kept for the retry, which will not file them twice": "them" should be "it" when `kept === 1`.
`ledgerKept` is incremented unconditionally once per flag, so it always equals `req.acceptDebt ? flaggedDebt.length : 0`; pass that expression to `withLedgerKept` and drop the mutable counter.

The two `try { … } catch (error) { throw withLedgerKept(error, ledgerKept); }` wrappers could be one around the whole `if (pullRequest) … else …` block, which would also cover `prBody` and the rest of the PR branch.

With the lfs clean filter emptied, a racy or stale-stat LFS file in the operator's checkout (real content) re-hashes as raw content, so `update-index --refresh` can no longer clear it and `read-tree -m -u` refuses the fast-forward as "not uptodate"; the failure is loud but the comment at L525 no longer holds for LFS paths.

Repos whose operator set `lfs.customtransfer.<name>.path`/`.args` and `lfs.standalonetransferagent` in local config (as lfs-folderstore and lfs-s3 setups instruct) now get refused at start, conductor and merge with "treat a session that wrote them as compromised" wording; decision 82 doesn't mention this cost.
The lfs-disarm test plants only a smudge marker; add one for `filter.lfs.process`, the path a global `git lfs install` actually configures and the least certain empty-value case.

Decision 82's git-lfs sentence "…and runs the program they name; so are the `lfs.extension.<name>.clean` and `.smudge` commands…" has no clear subject; rewrite as "and so are the … commands, which git-lfs runs on every lfs object".
Decision 82's "Tests:" paragraph has one line far longer than its neighbours, which wrap at about 100 columns like decisions 80 and 81.

The prBody comment "What the report answers for: GitHub can move the head after the gate read it back (decision 82)" restates assertPullRequestHead's JSDoc and can be deleted per AGENTS.md's duplicate-WHY rule.

assertPullRequestHead reads `headRefOid` through an inline cast plus a typeof-object guard and a nested ternary, where the same file types `ghJson` results with a named interface cast once (`ListedPullRequest`).

The new 'refuses a PR whose head is not the pushed sha' test hand-rolls an IIFE try/catch that returns the error message. The same diff adds the `refusalOf` helper (lines ~530-540) for exactly this. `refusalOf` sits inside the 'accepted debt and the refusals under the lock' describe, so the openPr test can't reach it. Hoisting it to the enclosing `runMergeGate` describe would let both reuse it.

The four new 'accepted debt and the refusals under the lock' tests each repeat the same seedSession + 700-line big.ts commit + mutating-gateCommands adapter setup; a small `adapterThatDoes(mutate)` factory would remove the repetition.

The PR edits the shared `fakeGh` helper (new `head` param, a `pr view` branch that runs `git ls-remote` against origin), so every existing `--pr` test now depends on it; "every existing test passes untouched" holds only for the `it(...)` bodies.

Every gh call runs with cwd set to the main checkout and no `-c` pins, and `gh pr create` runs `git status --porcelain` there, so a session-planted `core.fsmonitor` in the shared config could run unsandboxed during `pup merge --pr`; running gh from a neutral cwd (every call already pins `--repo`) would close it.
